title: Genetics Adventure 1: Chromosomes, genes and meiosis
welcome_lead: Today you'll halve a genome — meet meiosis and the origin of variation.
meta_desc: Biology Genetics — chromosomes, alleles, meiosis I & II, crossing over, independent assortment.
final_note: You learned meiosis halves the chromosome number, crossing over and independent assortment shuffle alleles, producing genetic variation.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Humans have 46 chromosomes — 23 pairs (22 autosomes + XX/XY).

Each chromosome is a single DNA molecule wrapped around histones into nucleosomes.

A karyotype displays them by size; trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) is detected this way.

Meiosis I separates homologous pairs:
- Prophase I — synapsis + crossing over at chiasmata.
- Metaphase I — bivalents align (independent assortment).
- Anaphase I — homologues separate.

Meiosis II separates sister chromatids (like mitosis). Result: 4 haploid cells.

Three mechanisms shuffle alleles in sexual reproduction:

1. Crossing over — new allele combinations on a chromosome.
2. Independent assortment — 2²³ possible gametes in humans (≈8.4 million).
3. Random fertilisation — any sperm meets any egg.

mcqs.q: Human diploid cells contain how many chromosomes?
How does myelination increase the speed of nerve impulse conduction?
options: Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.
Myelin contains additional ion channels that speed up depolarisation.
Action potentials jump between nodes of Ranvier (saltatory conduction), skipping the myelinated sections.
Myelin makes the axon thicker so the signal travels faster through more material.

mcqs.q: Where do plants get most of their biomass from?
options: Myelin contains additional ion channels that speed up depolarisation.
Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.
From carbon dioxide in the air — the carbon in plant tissue comes mostly from CO2 fixed during photosynthesis.
Plants get most of their mass from the soil through their roots.

mcqs.q: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker muscular wall than the right?
options: Myelin contains additional ion channels that speed up depolarisation.
It must pump blood at high pressure around the whole body; the right ventricle only pumps to the nearby lungs.
The left ventricle is thicker because it is on the same side as the brain.
The left ventricle is thicker because it handles oxygenated blood, which is harder to pump.
